sample_tweets.text: TAKING ADVANTAGE of NVIDIA HW GLITCH:  A researcher used voltage glitching to turn a cheap NVIDIA CMP 170HX 8GB mining card into something that outperforms a retail A100.  Kate (blog.kate.land) found a voltage fault injection vulnerability on the GA100 die. By glitching the fuse controller during boot with a custom STM32 board, she could arbitrarily blow fuses.  On NVIDIA’s GA100, blowing certain fuses can *relax* restrictions instead of tightening them. This let her unlock:  • Full ~80GB HBM on most 8GB cards (9/10 in her sample; one stopped at 64GB)   • 120–126 functional SMs (retail A100 ships with only 108)   • PCIe Gen4 x16   • NVLink (with a small hardware bridge + ROM check bypass)  Result: 85.9 TFLOP/s FP16 vs ~72.5 on a stock A100 (~1.18–1.2x faster), because the unlocked dies often have more working SMs than NVIDIA enabled for yield.  Software unlocks previously got people to ~64GB. This hardware approach clears the remaining floorsweeping and feature locks.  Disclosed to NVIDIA before publication. Tools and details are public. Not a simple mod — requires board work, a glitcher, and hours of attempts per card.
Do not confuse a design trade-off with a confirmed vulnerability. Security risk depends on a real trust boundary, an affected deployment, and a demonstrated consequence.

Microsoft has published a preliminary root cause for the Nov 12 global Microsoft 365 outage. A latent lock-contention defect in M365 networking gateway servers, introduced by a gateway-specific fix first deployed in July, is not present in broader Windows.  About 15 hours before the outage, Teams failed over to the primary gateway that also serves Exchange Online. About 14% of gateway capacity was already out of service from an unrelated issue. The failure cascaded during the US peak, and at its lowest more than 80% of servers were unresponsive. Bulkheads between partitions failed, so the impact spread globally.  Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint and Office failed out of the gateway and recovered first. Exchange Online could not fail out. Recovery was slow because returning servers were immediately overwhelmed. The preliminary report is in the Microsoft 365 admin center under MO1550821 and EX1550543. A final review is due later this week. This is an outage, not a cyberattack.  nitter.mie.foundation/clamanna/status/212220…

sample_tweets.text: 🚨 11-year-old Linux kernel flaw lets attackers remotely crash entire servers without authentication; CVE-2026-99288 Security researcher Hyunwoo Kim has disclosed NoisyTCP, a vulnerability affecting nearly all Linux distributions that allows unauthenticated attackers to crash servers running Nginx, Apache, and SSH using specially crafted TCP packets. The flaw exploits a race condition in the Linux kernel's TCP networking subsystem, triggering a kernel panic that can take down an entire host, including containers running on it. Researchers demonstrated crashes in as little as 5 seconds to 2 minutes on virtualized servers. The vulnerability has existed since 2015, and a patch was merged into the Linux kernel on November 3. Administrators are urged to apply updated kernels. Source: https:// github.com/V4bel/NoisyTCP
